C1.worst_defect: The hero tells me what it is and offers two clear buttons, but nowhere on the home page does it say who maintains it or who should not use it yet (for example a shop needing a cash drawer, integrated card terminal or iPad till). The only maturity signal is the small 'Pre-release · plugin 0.3.0' pill, and the footer says just 'MIT licensed. Built with TallyUI. For Medusa, see MedusaPOS.'

C2.worst_defect: Troubleshooting admits a dead end: for a refused till update with 'Any other code: the till has no retry or skip, and fixing the store does not make it send the update again. Sync now, signing out and in, and closing the register do not clear it.' and the log line 'does not come back'. The Limitations page, which is meant to list what it does not do, never mentions this register-data trap, so the honest-looking limits list is incomplete.

C3.worst_defect: The plugin's own 'New POS till key' button creates a vendurepos-pos-till role without ReadOrder, so every device-key till needs a manual role fix ('On plugin 0.3.0 the role it creates ... has the step 4 permissions except ReadOrder, so add ReadOrder to that role yourself'). The quick start documents a shipped tooling bug instead of the plugin fixing it, and a reader who skims past it gets a till whose order history is refused.
C3.where: quick-start 'Optional: a device key for each till' (quick-start.desktop.04); connect-a-till 'Create and use a device key'

C4.worst_defect: The changelog is written in internal protocol language a Vendure developer cannot act on: 'GET /tally/v1/info advertises order.create 1–5 (ADR 0005)', 'order.create v5 shipping ... refused as shipping_single (ADR 0005)'. The ADRs and the #116/#117 references are not linked. Separately, the refusal-with-no-recovery case sits only in Troubleshooting and is missing from Limitations, so the docs cross-link poorly on the riskiest behaviour.

C5.worst_defect: The home hero screenshot is cropped through a fourth row of product tiles, so half-tiles poke out at the bottom edge of the frame. The docs pages are a stock docs theme with a generic 'Copy Markdown / Open' toolbar on every page, which reads as default-looking rather than designed.
C5.where: home.desktop.01 hero image bottom edge; docs.desktop.01 toolbar

C6.worst_defect: Code blocks wrap rather than scroll on a 390 px screen, so the generateMigration call breaks over five ragged lines ('generateMigration(config, { name: / 'AddVendurePos', outputDir: / './src/migrations' }) ...'). That is hard to read and easy to mis-copy by eye. Everything else stacks cleanly, including the tax table, which turns into cards.

C7.worst_defect: The sitemap's lastmod stamps every URL within the last few hours of capture (2026-11-17T23:31 to 2026-11-18T10:13), which tells crawlers nothing. The SoftwareApplication JSON-LD carries no softwareVersion even though the site advertises plugin 0.3.0. Lighthouse 98/100/100/100, llms.txt, the search API and a real 404 are all fine.

overall_worst.defect: The site sells 'every sale lands in Vendure once' and keeps a candid Limitations page, but Troubleshooting reveals that a till update the store refuses with any code other than the two named ones can never be resent or cleared, and later register updates queue behind it. The Limitations page leaves this out. A sceptic who finds it buried in Troubleshooting stops trusting the Limitations list as complete, and would tell a client the register side is not production-safe.
overall_worst.where: troubleshooting.desktop.01 'Till updates line' bullet 'N till updates need attention'; limitations.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Add one bullet to Limitations, for example: 'A register update the store refuses (other than register_session_already_open or register_closure_number_invalid) cannot be resent from the till; later register updates for that register stay on the till', linking to the Troubleshooting section.
